clue.text: Shilling cut, save

parts.note: s. was the abbreviation for the old shilling
to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting note: trim a shilling off the bill and save money.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone or something is to rescue or exempt them from harm, a synonym of save.

clue.text: Assumption in force inspiring me after uprising

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: to prise is to force open

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An assumption gains strength and inspires the speaker after a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition taken as true for an argument, an assumption.

clue.text: Overrating gin, I stirred up a tonic

definitions.note: noun phrase; the answer is an adjective, as in 'tonic' meaning invigorating

indicators.note: stirring mixes things, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker who overrates gin mixes up a gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tonic' suggests the mixer for gin, but here it means restorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that restores vigour, so being one is to be refreshing and energising.

clue.text: Two tens added together for mark

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tally or result in a test or game

explanation.surface: Someone totting up two tens to arrive at a test mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old name for twenty, and also the points or grade awarded, as in a test result.

clue.text: Fast mover, one on the fiddle by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this phrase asks us to judge by what we hear when the words are spoken

parts.note: someone on the fiddle is cheating, a cheater; in non-rhotic speech the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: A violinist who plays fast, or a swindler working a quick scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is British slang for cheating or swindling, not playing a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, so a fast mover.

clue.text: Again deal with study before shift

indicators.note: before tells us which piece comes first in the finished word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: Revisiting a task: study first, then do your work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' sounds like a work period or a move, but here it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a matter is to tackle or attend to it once more.

clue.text: Audibly crude bellow

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: crude means raw, unrefined; in non-rhotic British speech the two sound the same

explanation.surface: Someone letting out a loud, vulgar shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is a loud deep cry, a bellow.

clue.text: Money excellent following strikes

indicators.note: following places the first-named piece after the second in the finished words

parts.note: to pound is to strike repeatedly
sterling means of excellent quality

explanation.surface: Workers win excellent pay after going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests industrial action, but it is a verb for hitting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounds sterling is the currency of the United Kingdom, a form of money.

clue.text: Paper uses it in circulation

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so these letters are turned about into new places

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper uses a story once it is in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, as in tissue paper or a paper handkerchief.

clue.text: Interval moments back, when lunch may be served?

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end towards its start

parts.note: moments are times
one o'clock is a typical lunchtime

explanation.surface: A musician pausing for a few moments before lunch is served.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition of ONE as a lunchtime hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest musical interval in Western scales, half of a whole tone.

clue.text: A river is a beauty

parts.note: taken as written
the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist's verdict that a certain river is a real beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' reads as the verb linking river to beauty, but it supplies its own letters; with no link word, the definition simply follows the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the handsome youth of Greek myth, is a byword for a beautiful young man.

clue.text: Retired minister is pocketing fifty coins

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing backwards, so the words are read in reverse
pocketing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Rev. is short for reverend, a minister
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman pocketing fifty coins from the collection plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is used collectively for coins made of silver or cupronickel, small change.

clue.text: Papers in sets in different order

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: ID means identity papers
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clerk filing papers in sets, putting them in a different order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is neatness, the state of being in good order.

clue.text: Single out character sometimes dropped in language

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the letter aitch is often dropped in speech, as in 'ello

explanation.surface: Singling out a letter that speakers sometimes drop in a certain language.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's character dropped in language is exactly H in English, which makes the clue neatly self-referential.
explanation.definitionFit: English is a language, the one spoken in England and widely across the world.

clue.text: On a grotty street feeling poorly

parts.note: on and in are interchangeable in phrases like on or in the team
taken as written
grotty is British slang for nasty or bad
a way is a road or street

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a grim, run-down street and feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Grotty is British slang for unpleasant or shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a bad way is an idiom for being ill or in poor condition.

clue.text: Guest at banquet missing starter — when chocolate's on the menu?

indicators.note: missing its starter means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: one who feasts is a guest at a banquet

explanation.surface: A diner skipping the starter at a banquet with chocolate on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the festival marked by chocolate eggs, so it is a time when chocolate is eaten.

clue.text: Ancient city quarter in South Africa

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a quarter is a part, a section of a whole

explanation.surface: An old city district located somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a city-state of ancient Greece, famed for its warriors.

clue.text: Lyrical image featuring every other part of forest

indicators.note: featuring means including, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

indicators.note: every other part means taking alternate letters and skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of forest

explanation.surface: A lyrical picture showing every part of a woodland scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic writing is expressive and musical, a synonym of lyrical.

clue.text: German bomb planted, dropped in

parts.note: the V-1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War
planted means placed or sited

explanation.surface: A wartime German bomb planted after being dropped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped in' sounds like the bomb falling, but it is the definition: called on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone is to pay them an informal call, to visit.

clue.text: Flesh is old in type of diagram

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first pieces go within the last

parts.note: a Venn diagram uses overlapping circles
taken as written
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A biology diagram explaining how old flesh is classified.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the meat of deer, a kind of flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Irish county finished with colleen

parts.note: done means finished
a colleen is an Irish girl, and gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: An Irish county that has seen the last of a local girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Colleen is the Irish word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the far north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Stop referring to injury

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a strain is a muscle injury

explanation.surface: A doctor's order to halt any mention of an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to hold them back or prevent them acting, to stop them.

clue.text: Prosaic activity of woodworm?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: drilling holes, which is what woodworm larvae do to timber

explanation.surface: A dry remark on how dull the life of a woodworm must be.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for tedious and a noun for making holes, as woodworm do in wood.

clue.text: Gang not allowed to be heard?

indicators.note: to be heard means judged by sound when spoken aloud

parts.note: something not allowed is banned, which sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A street gang told it may not be heard in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of people acting together, like a gang of robbers.

clue.text: Little time at the moment for insignificant player

parts.note: min is short for minute, a little time
now means at present

explanation.surface: A coach with little time left right now to field a weak player.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a tiny fish, so figuratively a small or unimportant competitor.

clue.text: Tonga is built around a capital city

indicators.note: around places the rebuilt letters on either side of the single remaining one
built means assembled from parts, so these letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Pacific island of Tonga building itself around a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Female creature scoffing last of quarry, a predator

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, so one piece is swallowed inside the other

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of quarry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A female animal gobbling up the remains of its prey, a predator at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore that hunts and scavenges, a predator.

clue.text: Nimble cartwheel, I gathered, in partial rotation?

indicators.note: rotating turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
gathered here means held within the run of words, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A gymnast admiring a nimble cartwheel, only half a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial' does double duty: only part of the words is used, and that part turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble are synonyms, both meaning quick and light in movement.
